title: 2154-cover-meets-robbins-betting-bounded-data
universal_lens: The Cover-Robbins mixture unifies adversarial game-theoretic probability with stochastic sequential analysis. By convexly blending uniform and modified Robbins priors over betting fractions, it achieves minimax O(ln n) worst-case regret while guaranteeing almost-sure O(ln ln n) regret on typical paths, establishing a universal duality between competitive optimization and asymptotic growth.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the affine-transformed profit stream into [0,1] to construct an anytime-valid wealth process. This serves as a rigorous Bayesian edge detector: if wealth exceeds 1/α, the engine's positive expected value is certified at level α without peeking corrections, providing a principled statistical trigger for scaling capital.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes the posterior mean of the Cover-Robbins mixture to dynamically compute the global stake multiplier bet-by-bet. This state-transition mechanism continuously adapts leverage based on realized outcomes, seamlessly integrating single-bet Kelly sizing with season-long bankroll management and automatic shutdown protocols.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by framing sports betting as a sequential decision problem over bounded data X_i \in [0,1]. The core objective is maximizing log-wealth, equivalent to minimizing regret R_n = \ln W^*_n - \ln W_n against the best constant betting fraction \lambda in hindsight. Pure Cover portfolios (uniform prior) guarantee O(ln n) worst-case regret but fail to exploit stochastic regularity. Conversely, Robbins-type mixtures achieve o(ln n) regret stochastically but suffer linear regret under adversarial sequences. The sovereign primitive emerges from a 50-50 convex combination of these priors. This mixture inherits the minimax O(ln n) protection from Cover while leveraging the Robbins component to achieve O(ln ln n) regret almost surely on measure-one sets E_0 where the Law of the Iterated Logarithm applies. The wealth process W_n acts as a non-negative supermartingale under the null hypothesis (no edge). By Ville's inequality, this constructs an anytime-valid confidence sequence. If the engine possesses true edge, W_n \to \infty; otherwise, it remains bounded with high probability. This dual nature provides both optimal asymptotic growth and a rigorous statistical test for model validity without requiring fixed sample sizes or peeking corrections.
